title: Oklahoma theaters, band split-up, and the offer to go to Yucatan
summary: After Devonport the band played theaters across Oklahoma until the group split up. Towles' father offered a Yucatan carnival job, and Morand sailed with him since others feared the Gulf.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: What about this experience of going to Mexico with the jazz band?

Well, that came up Nat Tolles' father as a bass player and also a cornet player. So, he had been writing Tolles. And when we'd come back to New Orleans, he had an engagement to go to Yucatan, married to Yucatan, Mexico, to play for the carnival season, which would last a week.

That was a sub year, around 1923. So, after we left Devonport, we started booking dances. After our contract was up, we started booking dances, playing theaters all over the state of Oklahoma. We got a booking agent, and we played such theaters like the Rialto in Tulsa. The first real theater I ever played in, and they gave us a nice write-up. It was crazy about the jazz band. And somehow, a lot of disincentions came from the band with the piano player. It caused the band to split up in Bristol, Oklahoma. We split up. Frank Pasley, he went to Chicago.

And we all split up. And Tolles and I, we were just coming back to New Orleans to make that trip with his father to go to Mexico. And we got as far as Shreveport, Louisiana, and by that time, Tolles had been bought a big 57-mile Cadillac. And the car broke down, and he wouldn't leave the car. So, I came home on the train, and I went to see his father. So, his father had difficulty in getting musicians to leave. They was afraid to cross the Gulf on the boat. So, I told him I would leave. So, I had to go to the doctor to be inspected and get passports and everything. So, I left with Nat Tolles' father flying up out in New Orleans. So, we crossed the Gulf and went into Progreso, Mexico. That's the harbor. And the custom officers. We had to catch a train from Progreso to go to Yucatan. At that time, it was a train, an engine that was going wood. And we had a time on that train. So, we played for a Yucatan club there, a real millionaires club.
